Separately, Fars reported Naqdi…
sources: Brig Gen Mohammad Reza Naqdi, senior adviser to IRGC commander-in-chief (speech, Oct 18); Fars News (reverse-engineering claim)
fault_line: Deterrence that keeps Washington honest — or empty bravado from a weakened Iran? (Echoes the MOAB-vs-missiles rhetorical arms race.)

sections.what_happened: Naqdi said Iran has prepared the 'father of missiles' — rhetorical answer to US MOAB ('mother of all bombs') threats — and that if the US miscalculates, 'entire infrastructure and energy investments belonging to regional rivals would be within striking distance'. Separately, Fars reported Naqdi claimed Iranian experts reverse-engineered a 14-ton US bomb dropped in the 12-day war ('now all the technologies of the 14-ton bomb have been analysed and are in our possession') and that Iran is preparing the 'father of missiles' for Washington.
sections.what_verified: The National (this morning) independently reports the Monday 'father of missiles' line; vietnam.vn/Dan Tri, dialoguepakistan, farazwire all carry the speech.
sections.what_disputed: FarazWire notes: 'father of missiles' is political/military rhetoric, NOT the confirmed name of a specific weapon — capability and readiness unestablished.
sections.why_matters: America waves the Mother of All Bombs; Tehran answers with the Father of Missiles — and names the region's energy infrastructure as the target.
sections.context: Background: Iran rhetoric — IRGC adviser Brig Gen Mohammad Reza Naqdi: 'father of missiles' ready to hit regional energy infrastructure; Fars claims Iran reverse-engineered 14-ton US bomb from 12-day war

totw_analysis: Our read: America waves the Mother of All Bombs; Tehran answers with the Father of Missiles — and names the region's energy infrastructure as the target. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Deterrence that keeps Washington honest — or empty bravado from a weakened Iran? (Echoes the MOAB-vs-missiles rhetorical arms race.)
